author: Baltimore City Wire
title: Bisciotti Family Foundation renews $3 million grant for Morgan State University scholarships
text:
Bisciotti Family Foundation renews $3 million grant for Morgan State University scholarships
A renewed investment of up to $3 million from The Bisciotti Family Foundation will expand the Ozzie Newsome Scholars Program at Morgan State University, according to a Sep. 2 announcement. The initiative aims to support talented Baltimore students by addressing unmet costs associated with college, such as tuition, textbooks, housing, transportation, and technology.
The eight-year grant will be managed through the Morgan State University Foundation and will provide scholarships of $15,000 annually for up to five years to 40 new Ozzie Newsome Scholars at Morgan—10 students in each of the next four incoming classes. This is the second award that Morgan has received from the Foundation for this program. Since its launch in 2022, 20 scholars have attended Morgan under this initiative, with its first two graduates celebrated in May 2025.
Endia M. DeCordova, vice president for Institutional Advancement at Morgan State University and executive director of the university's foundation, said: "This extraordinary, renewed commitment is both an investment in Baltimore's young people and a powerful affirmation of Morgan's ability to turn philanthropic trust into student achievement. We are deeply grateful to The Bisciotti Family Foundation for its ongoing confidence in our stewardship and in the success we have built together. Morgan will continue to manage these resources with care, accountability and an unwavering focus on helping every Ozzie Newsome Scholar persist, graduate and realize the promise of a Morgan education."
The Bisciotti Family Foundation will also continue honoring scholarship commitments at Bowie State University, Coppin State University and the University of Maryland Eastern Shore but plans to concentrate future cohorts at Morgan State for closer institutional partnership while maintaining support across Maryland’s Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs). Ravens owner Steve Bisciotti said: "Since its inception, the Ozzie Newsome Scholars Program has been about more than financial support. It honors Ozzie's legacy by investing in Baltimore students whose talent, determination and character continue to inspire us. We are proud of what these scholars have achieved and confident that Morgan State University will remain an exceptional partner in helping future scholars earn their degrees and impact Baltimore and beyond."
Scholarships can be used for tuition fees as well as other educational expenses including books or technical equipment; eligibility requirements include Pell Grant status along with graduation from a Baltimore City public school or approved independent school plus participation in CollegeBound’s College Completion Program.
Morgan State President David K. Wilson said: "Access to higher education should never depend on whether a promising Baltimore student can overcome every financial barrier alone... Donors such as The Bisciotti Family Foundation make those pathways real — giving students the freedom to focus on learning... This renewed commitment will change the trajectory not only of individual scholars but also their families."
